templates.template: Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI
templates.name: Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI
templates.description:
Netwatch - Active Directory Domain Controller checks (agentless WMI).
Provider: Netwatch.
Link this ONLY to domain controllers (or let the "Netwatch: link DC template" action link it automatically when DomainRole is 4/5). Requires "Windows by Netwatch WMI" also linked for OS metrics.

items.name: DC role WMI get
items.description: Raw Win32_ComputerSystem (Domain, DomainRole, Name) used to detect a domain controller.

items.name: Replication neighbors WMI get
items.description: Raw MSAD_ReplNeighbor rows: one per inbound replication partner and naming context. Needs Remote Enable on root\MicrosoftActiveDirectory. Disabled by default: enable it on DCs in domains with more than one DC.

discovery_rules.name: Domain controller role discovery
discovery_rules.description: Creates the domain controller checks only when Win32_ComputerSystem.DomainRole is 4 or 5. On member servers and workgroup hosts it discovers nothing, so the same template is safe on every Windows host.

item_prototypes.name: ATQ request latency
item_prototypes.description: Average time in milliseconds to process an LDAP request.

item_prototypes.name: ATQ outstanding queued requests
item_prototypes.description: LDAP requests waiting for a worker thread.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: LDAP request queue is building up
trigger_prototypes.description: More than {$AD.ATQ.QUEUE.MAX} LDAP requests have been queued for 15m. The DC cannot keep up with LDAP load (CPU, disk or expensive queries).

item_prototypes.name: AD log write latency
item_prototypes.description: Average time to write to the AD transaction log. High values slow every directory write.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: AD log write latency is high
trigger_prototypes.description: AD transaction-log write latency has been above {$AD.DB.LATENCY.MAX} ms for 15m.

item_prototypes.name: AD log writes per second
item_prototypes.description: AD transaction-log writes per second.

item_prototypes.name: AD database read latency
item_prototypes.description: Average time to read a page from the AD database (NTDS.dit). Sustained high values point to slow storage.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: AD database read latency is high
trigger_prototypes.description: AD database read latency has been above {$AD.DB.LATENCY.MAX} ms for 15m. The disk holding NTDS.dit is struggling; directory operations will be slow.

item_prototypes.name: AD database reads per second
item_prototypes.description: AD database page reads per second.

item_prototypes.name: AD database write latency
item_prototypes.description: Average time to write a page to the AD database.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: AD database write latency is high
trigger_prototypes.description: AD database write latency has been above {$AD.DB.LATENCY.MAX} ms for 15m.

item_prototypes.name: AD database writes per second
item_prototypes.description: AD database page writes per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS queries received per second
item_prototypes.description: Total DNS queries received per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS recursive query failures per second
item_prototypes.description: Recursive queries that failed per second (forwarders/root hints not answering).

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$AD.DNS.ENABLED}=1 and min(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.dns.recursive_fail_rate[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)>{$AD.DNS.RECURSIVE.FAIL.MAX}
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: DNS recursive query failures are high
trigger_prototypes.description: Recursive failures have been above {$AD.DNS.RECURSIVE.FAIL.MAX}/s for 15m. Check DNS forwarders and outbound UDP/TCP 53.

item_prototypes.name: DNS recursive queries per second
item_prototypes.description: Recursive queries per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS recursive timeouts per second
item_prototypes.description: Recursive queries that timed out per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS responses sent per second
item_prototypes.description: Total DNS responses sent per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS secure update failures (new)
item_prototypes.description: New secure dynamic update failures since the previous poll. Spikes usually mean clients cannot register their records.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$AD.DNS.ENABLED}=1 and sum(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.dns.secure_update_fail[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)>{$AD.DNS.SECURE.UPDATE.FAIL.MAX}
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: DNS secure update failures
trigger_prototypes.description: More than {$AD.DNS.SECURE.UPDATE.FAIL.MAX} secure dynamic updates failed in 15m.

item_prototypes.name: DNS dynamic updates received per second
item_prototypes.description: Dynamic update requests per second.

item_prototypes.name: DNS dynamic updates rejected (new)
item_prototypes.description: New dynamic updates rejected since the previous poll. Clients failing to register their DNS records.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$AD.DNS.ENABLED}=1 and sum(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.dns.updates_rejected[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)>{$AD.DNS.UPDATE.REJECT.MAX}
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: DNS dynamic updates are being rejected
trigger_prototypes.description: More than {$AD.DNS.UPDATE.REJECT.MAX} dynamic DNS updates were rejected in 15m. Clients may not be registering their records.

item_prototypes.name: DNS zone transfer failures (new)
item_prototypes.description: New zone transfer failures since the previous poll.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$AD.DNS.ENABLED}=1 and sum(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.dns.zone_transfer_fail[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)>0
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: DNS zone transfer failures
trigger_prototypes.description: Zone transfers from this server failed in the last 15m.

item_prototypes.name: DS directory reads per second
item_prototypes.description: Directory reads per second.

item_prototypes.name: DS threads in use
item_prototypes.description: Directory service threads currently in use.

item_prototypes.name: DS directory writes per second
item_prototypes.description: Directory writes per second.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP active threads
item_prototypes.description: LDAP threads currently servicing requests.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP bind time
item_prototypes.description: Time in milliseconds for the last successful LDAP bind.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: LDAP bind time is too high
trigger_prototypes.description: LDAP bind time has been above {$AD.LDAP.BIND.MAX} ms for 15m. Clients will see slow logons and slow application authentication.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP successful binds per second
item_prototypes.description: Successful LDAP binds per second.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP client sessions
item_prototypes.description: Number of connected LDAP client sessions.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: NTDS counters are not available
trigger_prototypes.description: No NTDS performance data for {$AD.NODATA_TIMEOUT}. WMI/DCOM is blocked, credentials are wrong, or the NTDS counters are missing on this host.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP negotiated binds per second
item_prototypes.description: LDAP binds using Negotiate (Kerberos or NTLM) per second.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP NTLM binds per second
item_prototypes.description: LDAP binds using NTLM per second.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP searches per second
item_prototypes.description: LDAP search operations per second.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP simple binds per second
item_prototypes.description: LDAP simple binds per second. Simple binds over port 389 send passwords in clear text.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP writes per second
item_prototypes.description: LDAP write operations per second.

item_prototypes.name: LSASS CPU usage
item_prototypes.description: CPU used by LSASS. Sustained high CPU can mean heavy authentication load or a spraying/brute-force attack.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: LSASS CPU usage is high
trigger_prototypes.description: LSASS has used more than {$AD.LSASS.CPU.MAX}% CPU for 15m. Check authentication load; an unusual spike can indicate an attack.

item_prototypes.name: LSASS handle count
item_prototypes.description: Open handles held by LSASS. A runaway count is an early sign of trouble.

item_prototypes.name: LSASS memory (working set)
item_prototypes.description: Memory held by LSASS. Steady growth can indicate a leak or a very large token/credential load.

item_prototypes.name: LSASS thread count
item_prototypes.description: Threads in the LSASS process.

item_prototypes.name: DRA inbound bytes per second
item_prototypes.description: Inbound replication traffic.

item_prototypes.name: Replication oldest successful sync
item_prototypes.description: Age of the stalest successful inbound sync across all links.

item_prototypes.name: Replication links
item_prototypes.description: Inbound replication links (partner x naming context) on this DC.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: Too few replication links
trigger_prototypes.description: This DC has fewer than {$AD.REPL.LINKS.MIN} inbound replication links. Set {$AD.REPL.LINKS.MIN}=0 in a single-DC domain.

item_prototypes.name: Replication links failing
item_prototypes.description: Links whose last sync failed or that have consecutive failures. Per-partner triggers are in the discovery rule.

item_prototypes.name: DRA outbound bytes per second
item_prototypes.description: Outbound replication traffic.

item_prototypes.name: DRA pending replication synchronizations
item_prototypes.description: Directory synchronizations queued on this DC but not yet processed.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: Replication backlog is growing
trigger_prototypes.description: More than {$AD.DRA.PENDING.MAX} replication syncs have been pending for 30m.

item_prototypes.name: NETLOGON share
item_prototypes.description: 1 if the NETLOGON share is published on this DC, 0 if missing.

trigger_prototypes.expression: max(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.share.netlogon[{#AD.DOMAIN}],#2)=0
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: NETLOGON share is missing
trigger_prototypes.description: The NETLOGON share is not published. The DC will not serve Group Policy/logon scripts and may not advertise as a DC. Check DFSR (SYSVOL replication) and the Netlogon service.

item_prototypes.name: SYSVOL share
item_prototypes.description: 1 if the SYSVOL share is published on this DC, 0 if missing.

trigger_prototypes.expression: max(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.share.sysvol[{#AD.DOMAIN}],#2)=0
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: SYSVOL share is missing
trigger_prototypes.description: The SYSVOL share is not published. The DC will not serve Group Policy/logon scripts and may not advertise as a DC. Check DFSR (SYSVOL replication) and the Netlogon service.

item_prototypes.name: Time offset
item_prototypes.description: Offset between this DC's clock and its time source. Kerberos fails when clocks differ by more than 5 minutes.

trigger_prototypes.expression: min(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.time.offset[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)>{$AD.TIME.OFFSET.MAX} or max(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.time.offset[{#AD.DOMAIN}],15m)<0-{$AD.TIME.OFFSET.MAX}
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: Clock is out of sync
trigger_prototypes.description: Time offset has been beyond +/-{$AD.TIME.OFFSET.MAX}s for 15m. Check W32Time: the PDC emulator should sync to an external NTP source, other DCs to the domain hierarchy.

item_prototypes.name: NTP time sources
item_prototypes.description: Number of NTP sources W32Time is currently using.

trigger_prototypes.expression: max(/Windows AD DS by Netwatch WMI/ad.time.sources[{#AD.DOMAIN}],30m)=0
trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: No active time source
trigger_prototypes.description: W32Time has had no usable time source for 30m. The clock is free-running and will drift.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP response time
item_prototypes.description: Time for the Zabbix server to open an LDAP session on port 389. Returns 0 when the service is down.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: Slow LDAP response
trigger_prototypes.description: LDAP connect time has been above {$AD.LDAP.RESPONSE.WARN}s for 5m.

item_prototypes.name: LDAP service (389)
item_prototypes.description: TCP/UDP check of LDAP (389) from the Zabbix server.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: LDAP (389) is not responding
trigger_prototypes.description: The last three checks of LDAP (389) failed. Clients cannot use this service on this DC.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: DNS (TCP 53) is not responding
trigger_prototypes.description: The last three checks of DNS (TCP 53) failed. Clients cannot use this service on this DC. Disable with {$AD.DNS.ENABLED}=0 if this DC does not run it.

discovery_rules.name: Replication partners discovery
discovery_rules.description: Discovers inbound replication partners (SourceDsaCN) from the MSAD_ReplNeighbor data.

item_prototypes.name: Replication from {#AD.PARTNER}: consecutive failures
item_prototypes.description: Highest NumConsecutiveSyncFailures across all naming contexts replicated from this partner.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: Replication from {#AD.PARTNER} ({#AD.PARTNER.SITE}) is failing
trigger_prototypes.description: Inbound replication from {#AD.PARTNER} has failed more than {$AD.REPL.FAIL.MAX} times in a row. Check 'Last result' for the error code, then run repadmin /showrepl on this DC.

dependencies.name: AD DS: No successful replication from {#AD.PARTNER} ({#AD.PARTNER.SITE})

item_prototypes.name: Replication from {#AD.PARTNER}: last result
item_prototypes.description: Win32 error code of the last sync from this partner. 0 = success. The first non-zero code across naming contexts is shown.

item_prototypes.name: Replication from {#AD.PARTNER}: time since last success
item_prototypes.description: Age of the stalest successful sync from this partner across its naming contexts.

trigger_prototypes.name: AD DS: No successful replication from {#AD.PARTNER} ({#AD.PARTNER.SITE})
trigger_prototypes.description: No successful inbound replication from {#AD.PARTNER} for more than {$AD.REPL.LASTSUCCESS.MAX}. Changes (passwords, group membership, GPOs) are not reaching this DC. If this approaches the tombstone lifetime the partner must be cleaned up.

macros.description: AD database/log I/O latency (ms) before alerting. NTDS.dit on slow disk drives this up.
1 if this DC runs the DNS Server role. Set 0 to silence DNS triggers.
Recursive DNS failures per second before alerting.
Secure dynamic update failures in 15m before alerting.
Rejected dynamic DNS updates in 15m before alerting.
